digest.key_takeaway: AWS has recently released File Mover Express, an open-source application under the Apache 2.0 license for transferring large files between local systems and Amazon S3. Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, it supports parallel transfers, automatic performance tuning, retries, pause and resume, and file integrity verification. By Renato Losio

articles.title: Will That AI Feature Actually Pay for Itself? Run the ROI Math First
articles.summary:
Every AI feature sounds like a money-saver in the pitch meeting. A chatbot will answer customers overnight, a writing tool will draft reports in seconds, and a smart search tool will end wasted time. Some of these ideas do pay for themselves. Many do not. The difference is rarely the technology. It is whether anyone ran the return-on-investment math before building.

Start with the cost side, and count everything, not just the obvious bill. First, add your API or token spend for a typical month, based on real usage, not the cheapest demo. Then add tool subscriptions, seats, and any extra data

articles.title: Kimi K2 closes in December: what moving to K3.1 Pro changes, and what the default reasoning effort costs
articles.summary:
TL;DR


Moonshot AI's documentation says that since 2026-10-31 the Kimi K2 series (kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code and its highspeed variant) is closed to newly registered accounts. Existing accounts keep working, and Moonshot plans to retire every K2 model by the end of December 2026. The named replacement is kimi-k3.1-pro. I did not call any API.
